summary.text: A 42-year-old male with poorly controlled seven-year type 2 diabetes managed solely with insulin, smoking one pack/day since age 19 and regular alcohol consumption developed left lumbar pain and a suspected upper urinary infection without initial imaging. A clinically identified retroperitoneal abscess secondary to complicated pyelonephritis extended through the left psoas and exteriorized at the left hip/thigh, prompting referral.

At admission he was alert and oriented, significantly malnourished with premature aging signs, hypoalbuminemia and inability to ambulate. The left thigh wound was large and bloody with mild purulent discharge, without necrosis/cellulitis; abdominal tenderness/masses were absent. Initial laboratory abnormalities included mild anemia, hypoglycemia and electrolyte disturbances. Renal function was described as normal despite the printed low creatinine/reference discrepancy. Urinalysis showed abundant bacteria and wound culture grew S. epidermidis. Separately, HIV/immunodeficiency testing was negative, with timing unspecified.

Admission electrolyte correction/nutritional support and IV piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g every six hours for 10 days accompanied initial caption-documented debridement and daily Dakin dressings for a week. NPWT lasted 12 days, then Dakin care resumed for one week, followed by a second 12-day NPWT course. After second removal, acetic acid dressings continued until discharge. Adequate granulation preceded dermatome skin grafting.

Authors report complete wound coverage in approximately five weeks and 90% STSG integration. Progressive functional recovery and absence of further infectious episodes occurred during a two-month hospitalization, ending in discharge for clinical improvement; exact graft date and discharge destination are unspecified.
